mappings.note: Which organisation presses for liberalisation of foreign trade and investment (the WTO) -- an institution among the factors that enabled globalisation, C-4.3-LO-1. Not LO-2: no effect on Indian producers or consumers is asked.
Removing government barriers is called liberalisation -- one of the enabling factors named in C-4.3-LO-1.

Which option refers to INVESTMENT -- a definitional item about the concept itself, so C-4.1 (recalls and understands economic concepts). Not LO-1, which needs investment to be treated as a driver of globalisation rather than defined.
Which is a BARRIER on foreign trade (an import tax) -- barriers and their removal are the mechanism behind globalisation, C-4.3-LO-1.
What Special Economic Zones are meant to attract (foreign companies and investment) -- a policy that enabled globalisation in India, C-4.3-LO-1.
Whom the entry of MNCs may harm (small and local producers) -- the impact on Indian producers, C-4.3-LO-2. Not LO-1: MNCs appear here as a cause of effects, not as an enabling factor.
Where Ford Motors set up its first Indian plant -- the chapter's worked example of an MNC operating in India and what it meant for local suppliers. C-4.3-LO-2.
Which industries were hard hit by foreign competition -- direct impact on Indian producers, C-4.3-LO-2.
The year India removed barriers on foreign trade and investment (1991) -- the policy turn that enabled globalisation here, C-4.3-LO-1.

Which option is NOT among the factors MNCs weigh before siting production -- cheap labour, skills, infrastructure, markets. These are the conditions that let production spread across countries, C-4.3-LO-1.
Why MNCs set up in more than one country -- to cut costs and reach markets. The mechanism of globalisation, C-4.3-LO-1.

The commonest route for MNC investment (buying up or partnering with local companies) -- how global production spreads, C-4.3-LO-1. The item that asks what the LOCAL company gains from such a partnership is mapped to LO-2 instead.
Removing barriers is liberalisation -- C-4.3-LO-1. A duplicate of an earlier item in this chapter; mapped consistently and flagged.
Entry of MNCs may harm domestic producers -- C-4.3-LO-2. Also a duplicate of an earlier item in this chapter.
Who has benefited LEAST from globalisation in India -- the uneven impact, which is the heart of C-4.3-LO-2.
The major benefit to a LOCAL company of joint production with an MNC -- capital and technology. An impact on Indian producers, C-4.3-LO-2, where the item about the MNC's preferred route sits at LO-1.
Which statement about the WTO is untrue -- the institution that pushes liberalisation, one of globalisation's enablers. C-4.3-LO-1.
What integration of markets means -- this is the definition of globalisation itself, the first clause of C-4.3-LO-1.
Which of the options contributes to globalisation -- the enabling factors, C-4.3-LO-1.
Investment means spending on assets such as land, buildings and machines -- a definition, so C-4.1. Mapped the same way as the other investment-definition item in this chapter.
How MNCs succeeded in entering global markets -- by investing, partnering and outsourcing. The mechanism of globalisation, C-4.3-LO-1.

What category the FDI drawn to India belongs to -- foreign investment as a driver of globalisation, C-4.3-LO-1. Not C-4.1: the item is about FDI's place in the globalisation story, not a bare definition of investment.
Which factor has NOT facilitated globalisation -- the enabling factors tested negatively, C-4.3-LO-1.
Globalisation has so far favoured whom -- the developed countries and the better-off. An evaluation of who gained and who did not, C-4.3-LO-2.
What cheaper imports plus weak infrastructure investment lead to -- damage to domestic producers. Impact, C-4.3-LO-2, not the enabling conditions of LO-1.
Which sector has NOT benefited from globalisation -- the uneven distribution of gains among Indian producers, C-4.3-LO-2.

What FAIR globalisation means -- benefits reaching everyone, including small producers and workers. This is the chapter's evaluative conclusion about impact, C-4.3-LO-2. Not LO-1: fairness is not an enabling factor.
